\section{Data records}
\label{sec:records}

Four product families are defined, and this release implements them to the maturity
reported in Table~\ref{tab:products}---which is not the same as four products shipping.
Stating which is which is the point of this section: a reader must be able to tell a
mass-conserving reconstruction from a declared allocation without reading the code. The
annual family is the reference configuration and the fiscal-year panel; the monthly family
is the monthly estimate on every annual cell; the spatial family is the spatial allocation
on administrative units and on the grid, with its unallocated remainder; the uncertainty
family is the parameter-level ensemble and the structural bridge. Every product is an
evidence-graded record: its rows carry the temporal and spatial evidence class of the
streams they aggregate, and the coverage matrix of Section~\ref{sup:coverage} states, per
module, which geometry the release holds and which classes dominate.

Two schema rules hold across all of them. Every published row states its reporting
period as explicit dates rather than an integer year, and the fiscal-start sectors'
filenames carry the period too. And every number a manuscript prints is checked against
the product it came from on every commit; a printed quantity with nothing behind it is a
build failure, not an editorial matter.
